backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, delete the third block of the A/B/X update (the third 'A = X @ X.transpose(1, 2)' through 'X = a * X + B @ X' group) so only two quintic iterations run. This cuts the Muon cost per step by about a third of its matmul work. Keep the target-magnitude normalisation unchanged. Check that the final orthogonalised update still has roughly unit singular values; if not, raise final_target_mag only if the accuracy drops.
backlog.title: Two Newton-Schulz iterations instead of three

backlog.spec: Replace the constant MUON_MOMENTUM in Muon.step with a ramp: momentum starts at 0.85 at step 0 and rises linearly to MUON_MOMENTUM (0.655 is the end value, so instead ramp from 0.5 up to 0.655 over the first 20 percent of total_train_steps, then hold). Implement by setting group['momentum'] from step_count / total_train_steps before the momentum multiply inside Muon.step. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Scale each filter's Muon update by a per-layer factor max(1, out_channels / in_channels) ** 0.5 (computed once in Muon.__init__ from reshaped_dims, stored in filter_params_meta). Multiply the orthogonalised update for that parameter by this factor before the foreach subtraction. This equalises effective step sizes between the wide 256-channel layers and the narrow 64-channel layer. Keep MUON_LR unchanged.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of all convolution and head weights during training: after each optimizer step, ema = 0.999 * ema + 0.001 * param, using torch._foreach_lerp_ or _foreach_mul_/_foreach_add_. Store ema tensors in a list created inside train() (fresh each run). In train(), at the end, copy the EMA values into the model parameters before returning, so predict() uses averaged weights. Use the decay only over the final 30 percent of steps (start EMA at step 0.7 * total) to avoid averaging in early high-loss weights.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for prediction

backlog.spec: Move the norm bias parameters (norm_biases list) and whiten bias out of the SGD optimizer into a torch.optim.AdamW group with lr = BIAS_LR * 0.1, betas (0.9, 0.99), weight_decay 0. Keep the head in SGD. The linear decay factor lr_factor1 should be applied to this AdamW group in the same way as the other groups. This tests whether an adaptive optimizer handles the tiny bias and norm-bias parameters better than SGD.
backlog.title: Nesterov SGD for biases replaced by Adam-style scaling on norm biases

backlog.spec: Replace the linear learning-rate decays lr_factor2 = 1 - step / total_train_steps (used for Muon and head) with a cosine: lr_factor2 = 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * step / total_train_steps)). Apply the same cosine shape to lr_factor1 for the whiten/norm bias group over whiten_bias_train_steps, clamped at zero. Keep all base learning rates identical. Compute the factors in Python with math.cos, which is already imported via math.ceil import (add 'import math').
backlog.title: Cosine decay instead of linear decay

backlog.spec: Multiply every learning rate by a warmup factor min(1, (step + 1) / warmup_steps) with warmup_steps = ceil(0.05 * total_train_steps), on top of the existing linear decay. Apply it in the training loop where lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 are computed, so the Muon and head groups ramp up over the first 5 percent of steps. This addresses the very large initial head and Muon steps early in training.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup then linear decay

backlog.spec: Keep the learning rate constant at its base value for the first 40 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to zero over the remaining 60 percent. Implement by replacing lr_factor2 = 1 - step * lr_factor2_base with lr_factor2 = min(1.0, 2.5 * (1 - step / total_train_steps)). Apply the same rule to lr_factor1 with whiten_bias_train_steps. This gives more time at high learning rate before annealing.
backlog.title: Flat-then-decay learning-rate schedule

backlog.spec: Reduce WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 0.05. The whiten bias receives gradients only while step < whiten_bias_train_steps, and with a shorter window the forward graph flips to whiten_bias_grad=False sooner. This saves a little backward work and changes which steps update the bias. No other edit is needed, because the existing code already handles the flag. Keep the bias learning-rate schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Stop whiten-bias training earlier

backlog.spec: Make the label-smoothing value depend on step: pass a Python float smoothing = LABEL_SMOOTHING * (1 - step / total_train_steps) into forward_step, and use it in F.cross_entropy. Since the value changes each step, avoid recompilation by passing it as a 0-dim CUDA tensor (torch.tensor(value, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)) and multiplying the cross-entropy target manually, or simply keep the constant and skip this idea if recompiles occur. The goal is to reduce label smoothing late in training, when the model should give sharp predictions.
backlog.title: Label smoothing annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Replace the alternating-epoch flip scheme in CifarLoader.__iter__ (images.flip(-1) when epoch % 2 == 1) with an independent random flip for each sample in every epoch. Apply batch_flip_lr to the cropped batch inside __iter__ after batch_crop, so each image is flipped with probability 0.5 on each pass. Keep the pre-flip cache logic only if needed for compile reasons; otherwise drop it.
backlog.title: Random per-sample horizontal flip

backlog.spec: Increase TRANSLATE from 2 to 3 so the padded images are 38x38 and batch_crop draws offsets in [0, 6]. Make sure predict()'s TTA still uses views consistent with the new padding: in infer's _get_tta_logits, derive the crops from the same pad size, or keep TTA pad at 1 as it is. This increases augmentation diversity across 7.65 epochs. Check whether the accuracy gain outweighs the slightly larger input cost.
backlog.title: Larger random translation with reflect padding

backlog.spec: After batch_crop and before color jitter, zero out one random 8x8 square per image in each training batch. Create the mask with random centre coordinates in [0, 32) using torch.rand, build a boolean mask with broadcasting over arange grids, and multiply the inputs by (1 - mask). Apply it inside CifarLoader.__iter__ before yielding batches so it runs in the compiled augmentation path. Fill value 0 in normalised space corresponds to the dataset mean.
backlog.title: Cutout regularisation

backlog.spec: Set the color_jitter config in train() to enabled False, so batch_color_jitter is skipped entirely. The brightness and contrast jitter costs a compiled kernel per epoch and may hurt a 7.65-epoch run that is underfitting rather than overfitting. This is a one-line config change and removes a source of noise from the input distribution.
backlog.title: Remove colour jitter

backlog.spec: In infer's _get_tta_logits, extend the views from the 3 shifted-and-base crops to a 5-view set: the original, reflect-padded crops at offsets (0,0), (0,2), (2,0), (2,2) and the centre. Concatenate them with their flips as before, and average the 10 logits. Keep the uncertain-quantile selection at 0.25, or try raising it to 0.5 if time allows. This is confined to predict() and does not affect training time.
backlog.title: Richer test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: In the tta function inside infer, drop the uncertainty selection and apply the mirror-and-shift averaging to every test image instead of only the 25 percent least confident. Set UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE to 1.0 so k_uncertain equals n. This spends a little more prediction time, but averaging can recover accuracy on confident images that were misclassified, and it removes the topk selection step.
backlog.title: Full test-time augmentation for all images

backlog.spec: Change widths in CifarNet from block1=64 to block1=48. The first ConvGroup has the largest spatial resolution, so reducing its width cuts a significant share of convolution FLOPs. Because conv2 of block1 and conv1 of block2 then take 48 input channels, all dependent shapes update automatically. Keep block2 and block3 at 256. This trades a little capacity for speed, and the other edits fix the curve.
backlog.title: Narrow the first block

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, add a skip connection around conv2: after norm2 and before the final activation, compute x = x + skip, where skip is the input to conv2 (the post-activation tensor from norm1 and SiLU). This needs the channel counts to match, which holds because conv2 maps channels_out to channels_out. Apply the activation after the addition. Only the forward method changes, and the BN parameters stay as they are.
backlog.title: Residual connection inside ConvGroup

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.layers, replace the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) with nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1) (after the last ConvGroup). The current feature map is 3x3 after three pools, so this keeps a spatial 1x1 output. Then in forward, the reshape x.view(len(x), -1) still works. Scale the head output by the same division by x.size(-1) as before, which now is 256. Test whether average pooling generalises better than max pooling at this depth.
backlog.title: Global average pool instead of final max pool

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.__init__, change self.activ = nn.SiLU() to self.activ = nn.GELU(). The network already starts with nn.GELU() in CifarNet.layers, so the change just makes the block activations match. This is a minor change in curvature that may improve convergence speed at the same cost. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Replace SiLU with GELU in blocks

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed division by x.size(-1) in CifarNet.forward with a learnable scalar parameter head_scale initialised to 1/x.size(-1) = 1/9 (use 1/9 directly because the feature map has size 9 after pooling? check the flatten size first and use 1/size). Register it as nn.Parameter with requires_grad True. Include it in the SGD head group with the head learning rate and no weight decay. This gives the optimizer control over the output logit scale.
backlog.title: Learnable head scale

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and multiply BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(1024 / 1536) = 0.816. The loss uses reduction sum, and the optimizer already scales with batch-size-weighted decay (wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * batch size), so the weight decay term is recomputed automatically. This gives more optimizer steps per epoch and may improve the per-epoch sample efficiency, at the cost of more kernel launches.
backlog.title: Batch size 1024 with scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 2048 and multiply BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(2048 / 1536) = 1.155. Keep all other settings the same. Larger batches reduce per-step overhead, which matters because a 7.65-epoch run has only a few hundred steps and launch overhead is significant. Note that drop_last keeps only full batches, so the epoch step count shrinks slightly.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: Instead of shuffling every epoch with torch.randperm, shuffle once per two epochs and reuse the permutation on the following epoch but with the flip applied differently. This reduces the randperm and gather work per epoch. Implement by only calling torch.randperm when epoch % 2 == 0 in CifarLoader.__iter__, and keep self._indices unchanged on odd epochs. Data order is still random across epochs because augmentation changes.
backlog.title: Gradient-free batch shuffling per epoch with fixed chunks

backlog.spec: In Muon.step, the momentum buffers are kept in half precision (momentum_buffer_dtype=torch.half) and cast to and from the gradient dtype each step, creating extra copies. Set the optimizer's momentum_buffer_dtype to match the parameter dtype (half already, so simplify the branch by always using the direct foreach path and removing the grad_casts list). This reduces intermediate allocations in the compiled step. Behaviour should match exactly.
backlog.title: Remove momentum buffer half-precision cast

backlog.spec: Wrap the per-step parameter update of optimizer1 and optimizer2 (the foreach adds, multiplies, and the learning rate factor assignments) in a torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead') function that takes the current learning rates as 0-dim CUDA tensors. Use tensors for lr so the graph does not recompile when the value changes. This removes Python dispatch overhead across the roughly few hundred optimizer steps per run. Compilation happens before timing, so it is free at run time.
backlog.title: Compile the optimizer update with CUDA graphs

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.init_whiten, replace torch.svd(est_patch_covariance) with torch.linalg.eigh(est_patch_covariance), which is symmetric. Eigenvalues come back ascending, so reverse the order: S = S.flip(0), U = U.flip(1). Then the rest of the function is unchanged. This is a small speed-up in the timed setup and avoids the deprecated svd path, and it is numerically equivalent for symmetric covariance.
backlog.title: Switch whiten initialisation to eigh

backlog.spec: In infer_basic and the tta function, remove the .clone() calls after model(inputs) and model(inputs_batch) in the non-TTA paths, since the outputs are consumed by torch.cat and softmax and do not share storage with the model. Keep the clone only where a view could alias a buffer that later gets overwritten. This removes a copy of the 10000x10 logits per call, which is tiny but free to remove.
backlog.title: Remove the unnecessary clone in inference

backlog.spec: Inside _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, cast the stacked matrix X to torch.bfloat16 before the iteration loop and cast the result back to half afterwards. A4000 Ampere tensor cores run bf16 matmuls at speed comparable to fp16, and bf16 has a larger exponent range, which avoids overflow in the repeated A @ A products. Keep the normalisation steps in half. Verify that the orthogonalised update norms match the fp16 version within a few percent before accepting the change.
backlog.title: Mixed-precision Newton-Schulz in bfloat16

backlog.spec: Keep the step count fixed at EPOCHS * len(train_loader). Keep a per-sample loss vector of length 50000 on the GPU, initialised to 1.0. Change forward_step to return per-sample losses (reduction none), sum them for backward, and write the detached losses back into the vector at the batch indices after each step. At the start of each epoch, draw 50000 indices with torch.multinomial, with replacement, using weights equal to the stored loss raised to the power 0.5. Chunk them into batches of BATCH_SIZE as before. Flip, translate and jitter stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Loss-weighted hard-example sampling

backlog.spec: For the first 50 percent of optimizer steps, feed random 28x28 crops taken from the augmented 32x32 batch, using the existing batch_crop logic with crop size 28. Switch to full 32x32 images for the remaining steps. The spatial chain 28 to 27 to 13 to 6 to 3 to 1 still ends at 1x1, so the head shape is unchanged. Compile each shape once, with dynamic=False. The learning-rate schedule and the 32-pixel test-time path stay as they are.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution with 28-pixel crops early

backlog.spec: In the training loop, for each batch with probability 0.25, and only while step is below 70 percent of total_train_steps, apply CutMix. Permute the batch, sample lam from a Beta(1,1) distribution, paste a rectangle covering about (1 minus lam) of the image area from the permuted batch at a random centre, and set the targets to the two label distributions weighted by the actual pasted area. Compute the loss as the weighted sum of the two cross-entropy terms, with label smoothing kept. All other batches are unchanged.
backlog.title: CutMix on a fraction of batches

backlog.spec: Move the head weight out of the SGD group and into a second Muon optimizer. Treat it as a 10 by 256 matrix, with the same Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation, momentum and weight decay as the conv filters. Give it its own learning rate, HEAD_LR scaled by 0.1 as a starting point, with the same linear decay to zero. Keep the output scaling by 1 over the feature width unchanged. The biases stay on Nesterov SGD.
backlog.title: Muon on the classifier head

backlog.spec: After the Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation of each filter, track an exponential moving average of the squared row norms of each update, with decay 0.95, separately for each filter. Divide each update row by the square root of its running average, then rescale the whole update so its Frobenius norm matches the unnormalised orthogonalised update. This equalises the step size across output channels. The learning rate and momentum stay the same.
backlog.title: Row-normalised Muon updates (NorMuon-style)

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, replace the MaxPool2d(2) after conv1 with a learned stride-2 3x3 convolution from channels_in to channels_out, with padding 1 and no bias. Keep the rest of the group as is, so the norm, activation and conv2 order is unchanged. The layer that follows the group then takes stride-2 features. Make the first group's stride-2 conv operate on the whitened input as before. Initialise the new stride-2 convolution with the same Dirac scheme used for the existing convolutions, applied to the first channels.
backlog.title: Stride-2 convolution replaces the block max-pool

backlog.spec: Replace the compiled forward_step with a torch.compile mode reduce-overhead version, or capture forward plus backward with torch.cuda.graphs on static input and label buffers that are copied into at each step. Keep the optimizer calls outside the graph. Capture after the first step so warm-up is done, and reuse the graph for all remaining steps of the run. The last partial batch is already dropped, so the static shapes hold. Recreate the graph at the start of each train() call, because a run must start from scratch.
backlog.title: CUDA-graph capture of forward and backward

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 3072 and scale the learning rates for the conv filters and the biases by the square root of 2 relative to 1536, with the head LR scaled the same way. Keep EPOCHS, the momentum values and the weight-decay formula unchanged, since wd is already multiplied by the batch size. This halves the number of optimizer steps. Recheck the whiten-bias step count, which is derived from len(train_loader) and so scales automatically.
backlog.title: Batch size 3072 with scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: At the start of each epoch, shuffle the indices within each of the 10 classes separately, then interleave them so that every batch of BATCH_SIZE contains the same number of samples from each class, with a small random remainder. Build the epoch order on the GPU with torch.randperm per class and a single reshape. Keep the augmentation and the learning-rate schedule unchanged. The aim is to remove batch-to-batch label-count variance in the gradient.
backlog.title: Class-balanced stratified batches

backlog.spec: In predict, replace the separate initial pass and the uncertain-image pass with one forward over the stacked views of all test images, computed in a single compiled call with batch size 2000. Keep the 25 percent selection by confidence, but compute it from the first view's logits inside the same graph, and select the rows after the fact with torch.where instead of index assignment. The model is still not changed, and the output shape stays (N, 10). This removes the Python splitting and the extra copies.
backlog.title: Half-precision test-time pass in one fused batch

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.init_whiten, keep only the top K eigenvectors (e.g. K=12, so whiten_width = 12 instead of 24) by sorting S descending and slicing U before building eigenvectors_scaled, then build the whiten weight from the K kept filters and their negations (or just the K filters if the negation trick is dropped). Set whiten_width in __init__ to match. Everything downstream (ConvGroup input channels) follows from whiten_width. This removes the lowest-variance patch directions, cutting first-block compute and memory traffic while keeping most of the signal.
backlog.title: Truncated PCA whitening to fewer channels

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.layers, delete the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) so the last ConvGroup output is 256 x 3 x 3. Change the head to nn.Linear(256*3*3, 10, bias=False). In forward, x.view(len(x), -1) already flattens, and the division by x.size(-1) becomes division by the new flattened size, so keep that scaling. The head then sees spatial information it currently discards; the cost increase is confined to the 2304-by-10 linear layer and a slightly larger final norm and activation.
backlog.title: Remove final MaxPool and flatten the 3x3 map into the head

backlog.spec: Replace nn.SiLU() in ConvGroup (both self.activ uses) with a ReLU-squared module: forward returns F.relu(x).square(). Keep the first GELU in CifarNet.layers unchanged. ReLU-squared is cheaper than SiLU (no sigmoid) and has a sharper, sparser response that may suit the short training budget. Batch norm without learned scale sits before each activation, so the output scale is controlled by the norm layers. No other changes are needed.
backlog.title: ReLU-squared activation in the blocks

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, remove norm1 (the BatchNorm after the pooled conv1) and its use in forward, so the path is conv1, pool, SiLU, conv2, norm2, SiLU. The 'norm' name filter for bias training still picks up norm2 only. This removes one normalisation pass per block, which cuts memory traffic in each of the three blocks. The later norm2 still normalises each block output, so the network stays well conditioned. Keep the whiten bias and head groups as they are.
backlog.title: Drop the first BatchNorm in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.forward, when self.training is true, apply nn.functional.dropout2d (channel-wise, p=0.1) to the output of the whitening convolution, before self.layers. In eval mode it is a no-op, so predict is unchanged. The 24 whitened channels are highly redundant (they come in +/- pairs), so dropping whole channels forces the network to use all of them and acts as a cheap regulariser. Keep the rest of the training loop identical.
backlog.title: Channel dropout on the whitened input during training

backlog.spec: At the end of train(), after the last optimizer step, switch to eval-free statistics collection: set every BatchNorm layer's momentum to None (cumulative average), reset its running_mean and running_var, then run one no-grad pass over the unaugmented normalised training images in batches of 2000 with model.train() so the running statistics match un-jittered, un-flipped, un-cropped data. Then return. Training-time running stats are averaged over augmented, cropped batches, so this corrects a mismatch that matters for the test-time views. The pass is cheap and is inside the timed train() call.
backlog.title: Post-training batch-norm recalibration on clean images

backlog.spec: In train(), after the final two epoch boundaries, store a deep copy of the model's state_dict (copy.deepcopy of the parameters and buffers, or clone each tensor) at each of those points, held in a module-level list that is cleared at the start of train(). In predict(), run the existing inference on the live model and on each stored snapshot via torch.func.functional_call or by loading the snapshot into a separate model instance created in make_model, then average the softmax outputs or logits. predict must not change the trained model, so use a separate copy for the snapshots. Snapshots are built from training data only, so the harness rules hold.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble of the last two epochs in predict

backlog.spec: Train the first half of the steps with batch size 768 (learning rates for the Muon and SGD groups scaled by sqrt(768/1536) at those steps, and whiten-bias steps counted in samples rather than batches), then switch to batch size 1536 for the rest. Implement by making the CifarLoader batch size a function of the step and keeping every batch shape static (two shapes only), so forward_step with dynamic=False compiles once per shape. The untimed warm-up call runs the same code path, so both shapes are compiled before timing. Total epochs and total optimizer steps should stay consistent with EPOCHS by recomputing total_train_steps from the sample count.
backlog.title: Progressive batch size from 768 to 1536

backlog.spec: Keep a per-sample loss buffer of length 50000 created inside train() (not reused across runs). Use forward_step with reduction='none' to get per-sample losses, store them for the indices in the current batch, and record them with .detach(). From epoch 2 on, at the start of each epoch drop the 10 percent of samples with the lowest stored loss from that epoch's permutation, so the epoch has 45000 samples and fewer optimizer steps. Recompute total_train_steps from the reduced epoch length so the linear decay still reaches zero. The rule is data-driven within a run only, so no state leaks across runs. This is a hard-example style speedup that trades a little easy-data signal for compute.
backlog.title: Skip the easiest 10 percent of images each epoch

backlog.spec: In train(), when building optimizer2, split the filter parameters into the three ConvGroup stages and give each a learning-rate multiplier: 1.3 for block1, 1.0 for block2, 0.75 for block3 (the multipliers are applied through param groups, with group['initial_lr'] set to MUON_LR times the multiplier so the existing per-step linear decay factor still applies). Keep the same momentum, norm_freq and weight decay in every group. The Muon step loops over self.param_groups[0] today, so the Muon class must be adjusted to iterate over all groups or the three stages must be passed to a single group with per-parameter lr scaling. The intent is to adapt step size to the scale of each stage's features.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled Muon learning rate multipliers

backlog.spec: In training, make BatchNorm compute batch statistics over fixed sub-batches of 512 samples instead of the full 1536 batch. In the BatchNorm forward, when self.training, reshape the input from (B, C, H, W) to (B/512, 512, C, H, W) (or (B/512, 512*H*W) layouts as convenient), compute mean and variance per chunk, normalise, and reshape back. Keep running_mean and running_var updated as the average over chunks, and keep eps=1e-12, the frozen weight and the learned-free bias unchanged. Eval mode is untouched. Do not change any other hyperparameter. The goal is extra noise regularisation from smaller normalisation groups at no extra FLOPs.
backlog.title: Ghost batch norm with 512-sample statistics

backlog.spec: In predict(), combine the flipped and shifted views by averaging softmax probabilities rather than raw logits, then return log of the averaged probabilities so the output stays a logit-like tensor of shape (N, 10). Apply this in infer's tta_level==2 path, in both the uncertain-image pass (_get_tta_logits) and the initial pass, so each image's final vector is the mean of per-view softmax outputs. Keep the same views, the same 25 percent uncertainty selection, and the same model. Only the aggregation changes.
backlog.title: Average softmax probabilities across TTA views

backlog.spec: Keep a per-sample buffer of the model's soft predictions from the previous visit to each training image. Allocate it inside train() at the start of each run (for example a (50000, 10) half or float tensor filled with zeros, plus a validity mask), so nothing carries between runs. During each training step, store the detached softmax of the current logits into the buffer at the batch indices, after the forward pass. From the second half of training onward, replace the hard label-smoothed target with a mixture: 0.5 times the smoothed label plus 0.5 times the stored previous-epoch softmax, for samples whose buffer entry is valid. The cross-entropy with reduction sum is then computed against these soft targets. Keep the optimizers, the schedules and the augmentations unchanged.
backlog.title: Self-distillation from the previous epoch's predictions

backlog.spec: Change the fixed whitening layer from 2x2 to 3x3 patches. Set whiten_kernel_size = 3 in CifarNet.__init__, so whiten_width becomes 2*3*9 = 54 channels, and the first ConvGroup takes 54 input channels. init_whiten already reads the kernel size from self.whiten.weight.shape, so it adapts; with padding 0 the spatial size drops from 31 to 30 before the first block, so keep the existing max pool and the final MaxPool2d(3) ordering consistent (30 pooled to 15, then 7, then the final pool of 3 gives 2) and adjust the final pool to what gives a valid flatten into the 256-wide head. Keep the eigen-whitening, the sign-paired initialisation and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Three-by-three whitening patches

backlog.spec: Replace the nn.Linear head with a cosine classifier. L2-normalise the 256-dimensional pooled features and the 10 class weight vectors, take their dot products, and multiply by a learnable scalar scale initialised to 10 (a single parameter, given the head learning rate group and no weight decay). Keep the existing head LR and the 1/x.size(-1) scaling replaced by this scale. Keep the reset() behaviour sensible: reset_parameters for the head weight should use the same normal init, and the learnable scale is reset to its initial value in reset(). Everything else, including label smoothing and the head's SGD group, stays the same.
backlog.title: Cosine classifier head with learnable temperature

backlog.spec: Change how Muon sees 4-D convolution filters. Instead of reshaping a weight of shape (out, in, 3, 3) to (out, in*9) and orthogonalising that matrix, reshape it to (out*3, in*3), i.e. treat each row-tap pair as a matrix of size out-by-in per kernel row, or equivalently orthogonalise the (out, in) matrix of each of the 9 spatial taps separately by permuting to (9, out, in) and batching. Implement this inside the Muon meta data: store the permutation and pad to the larger shape used by _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, then un-permute after the Newton-Schulz step. Keep the norm-scaling rule, the LR, the momentum and the weight decay as they are.
backlog.title: Orthogonalise each 3x3 conv per spatial tap

backlog.spec: Remove per-batch augmentation calls from the training loop. At the start of each epoch in CifarLoader.__iter__, apply the flip, the 2-pixel reflect-pad crop and the brightness and contrast jitter to the full 50000-image set in one compiled call, producing a fresh augmented tensor of shape (50000, 3, 32, 32) in half precision (this is about 300 MB, acceptable). Then yield contiguous slices of that tensor for each batch rather than gathering with idxs each step. The random permutation is applied once to the augmented tensor, or equivalently to the labels together with the images. Keep the 28-pixel early crops applied per batch as they are, since they are part of the speed gain from the accepted change. The goal is to remove launch overhead from the inner loop without changing the augmentation distribution.
backlog.title: Whole-epoch augmentation in one compiled call

backlog.spec: Replace the plain label-smoothed cross-entropy in forward_step with a focal-style loss that multiplies each sample's loss by (1 - p_true) raised to gamma = 0.5, where p_true is the softmax probability of the true class computed from the same logits, detached so the modulating factor carries no gradient. Keep the label smoothing applied inside the base cross-entropy and keep reduction sum. Use the same loss scale as before so the optimizer LRs need no change. The aim is to slightly down-weight already-confident examples and put more gradient on hard ones, a mild alternative to hard-example sampling.
backlog.title: Mild focal modulation on the cross-entropy

backlog.spec: Change predict() so the BatchNorm layers normalise with the statistics of the test batch being scored (train-mode normalisation), while leaving the stored running_mean and running_var untouched. Implement this by setting the BatchNorm modules to train mode in a predict-only context, with momentum set to 0 so running buffers do not change, or by computing the batch mean and variance explicitly in a forward hook. Use batches of 2000 test images as now. The model parameters and buffers must be unchanged after predict, so verify that the buffers are restored. Keep the TTA views and the 25 percent uncertainty rule as in the current predict.
backlog.title: Batch-statistics BatchNorm at test time without updating state

backlog.spec: Insert a dropout layer with p = 0.1 between the final flatten in CifarNet.forward and the head linear layer, active only in training mode (nn.Dropout does this automatically in eval). Keep the head weight scaling and the head SGD group unchanged, and keep the same flatten and contiguous call. Apply it inside the compiled forward_step, so it is fused with the head matmul. No other regularisation changes, and the label smoothing value stays at 0.09. The purpose is a light regulariser on the 256-dimensional feature vector that the head sees, at zero extra cost to the blocks.
backlog.title: Dropout on pooled features before the head

incumbent.description: Feed random 28x28 crops (via the existing batch_crop) for the first half of optimizer steps and full 32x32 images afterwards, with the forward step compiled with dynamic=False so each shape compiles once.

memo:
Helped: only slot 7, random 28x28 crops for the first half of optimizer steps (cost -0.0601, delta -0.0768 vs incumbent, 1 run). It cuts per-step compute, so it is a speed gain. Single run, noise sd about 0.026, so replicate before stacking.

Did not help: structural changes (conv2 residual skip +0.2176; head to Muon +5.3473; removing the final pool crashed twice), schedule changes (flat-then-decay +0.4503; warmup +0.1187), and optimizer tweaks (NorMuon +0.0450). Colour jitter off was +0.0333. Neutral within noise: richer TTA +0.0021, momentum ramp +0.0061, label smoothing anneal +0.0189. Batch 1024 with scaled LRs was +0.0579. Translation 3 px was -0.0099 vs incumbent, a small gain within noise.

Next: replicate slot 7. Then try progressive resolution variants: smaller crops for longer, or a gradual size ramp. Look for other changes that cut per-step cost. Avoid architecture, schedule and optimizer edits.
